graph.summary: Tamoxifen → 4-Hydroxytamoxifen → Estrogen receptor alpha → cell proliferation → Breast Cancer

evidence.snippet: Tamoxifen requires enzymatic activation by cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes for the formation of active metabolites 4-hydroxytamoxifen and endoxifen.
evidence.explanation: Tamoxifen is metabolised by CYP enzymes to form the active metabolite 4-hydroxytamoxifen.

evidence.snippet: both metabolites have an approximately 100-fold greater affinity for the estrogen receptor and the ability to inhibit cell proliferation
evidence.explanation: 4-Hydroxytamoxifen binds estrogen receptor alpha with ~100-fold greater affinity than tamoxifen and inhibits its activity.

evidence.snippet: 4-hydroxytamoxifen and endoxifen, which have 30- to 100-fold greater affinity to the estrogen receptor and the potency to suppress estrogen-dependent breast cancer cell proliferation
evidence.explanation: Active tamoxifen metabolites including 4-hydroxytamoxifen have high affinity for the estrogen receptor and suppress its proliferative activity.

paper.title: Pharmacogenomics of tamoxifen: roles of drug metabolizing enzymes and transporters.

evidence.snippet: About two thirds of breast cancers in women are hormone-dependent and require estrogen for growth, its effects being mainly mediated through estrogen receptor alpha (ERalpha).
evidence.explanation: Estrogen receptor alpha mediates estrogen-driven growth of hormone-dependent breast cancer cells.

paper.title: Docosahexaenoic acid induces proteasome-dependent degradation of estrogen receptor alpha and inhibits the downstream signaling target in MCF-7 breast cancer cells.

evidence.snippet: RBCK1 regulates cell cycle progression and proliferation of ERalpha-positive breast cancer cells by supporting transcription of ERalpha and cyclin B1
evidence.explanation: ERα supports cell cycle progression and proliferation in ER-positive breast cancer cells.

paper.title: RBCK1 drives breast cancer cell proliferation by promoting transcription of estrogen receptor alpha and cyclin B1.

evidence.snippet: inhibit tumor cell proliferation by targeting ER signaling
evidence.explanation: Endocrine therapies treat breast cancer by inhibiting tumor cell proliferation, demonstrating that cell proliferation contributes to breast cancer.

paper.title: Clinical Challenges in the Management of Hormone Receptor-Positive, Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2-Negative Metastatic Breast Cancer: A Literature Review.
